author: Plato
title: The Republic of Plato
edition: Benjamin Jowett translation, The Republic of Plato: An Ideal Commonwealth, revised edition (The Colonial Press, copyright 1901; Wikisource scan index identifies London, 1901). Translation year identifies this printed English edition, not Jowett’s first translation. Direct scan-backed Wikisource transcription of Books VI–VII; no Lawton introduction, illustration captions, or Jowett introductory matter is included. Prose wrapping is collapsed within preserved paragraphs, HTML emphasis becomes plain text, and printed page numbers, footnote references, and zero-width page-boundary characters are omitted. Main-text wording, punctuation, and apparent source transcription errors are retained; no claim of a fresh complete print-image collation is made. The library text holds the whole dialogue, Books I to X, each under its printed book title, with the persons of the dialogue and every quotation; the frontispiece, title page, Lawton's Special Introduction, the Introduction subpage are omitted; the 117 footnotes are kept, each anchor as [n] in the transcription's numbering, which restarts in each book, and each note as a paragraph [Footnote n: text] after its book's text, where the Wikisource transcription lists them. As in the nightly selections, the few quotations the transcription sets line by line (verse and the displayed proportion in Book VII) are folded into paragraphs like the prose. On 2026-11-18 four passages outside Books VI and VII (Book I from Thrasymachus’ outburst to his ruler “in so far as he is a ruler”; Book III from the “needful falsehoods” to the end of the book; Book VIII from the democratic man to the rise of tyranny; Book X from the souls’ arrival before Lachesis to the end) were collated word by word against the OCR of Internet Archive cu31924032626446 (this Colonial Press edition) and compared with Project Gutenberg 1497, each difference decided on the page images: two readings changed, the semicolon after “of the stronger” in Book I (page 15), which the print sets outside the closing quotation mark, and “may deceive the rulers” in Book III (page 101), where the transcription has a comma after “deceive” for a blot on the page. Later on 2026-11-18 four further passages (Book I from the opening to Cephalus’s departure; Book IV from “after much tossing” to “let us not faint by the way”; Book V from “Let me next endeavor” to the dreamer and the man “wide awake”; Book IX from the image of the many-headed monster to the end of the book) were collated the same way against cu31924032626446 and Project Gutenberg 1497: one reading changed, the colon after “threshold of old age” in Book I (page 3), which the print sets outside the closing quotation mark, and in the same paragraph a stray space before the colon of “I replied:” was closed up.

rights.basis: This identified English Jowett edition bears The Colonial Press copyright 1901 and is linked to its complete scanned print witness. Its English text was published before 1931 and is public domain in the United States as of 2026; the rights claim does not rely on the ancient Greek original. No modern editorial material is included.

acquisition.method: Wikisource rendered page HTML (index.php action=render) for the ten book subpages in printed order, The Republic of Plato/Book 1 to Book 10 (revisions 10050435, 10050449, 10050452, 10050454, 10050424, 10074709, 11985126, 10368554, 12283625, 12283635); downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the ten responses concatenated in that order and downloadUrl the first of them. Only the transcluded scan text is used: Wikisource headers, page-number anchors and zero-width page-boundary characters removed; the work title and each book's number and title became headings; everything else, including table rows of the persons list and centred or line-set quotations, became paragraphs with whitespace and line breaks collapsed to single spaces; emphasis flattened; footnote calls kept as [n] in Wikisource's per-subpage numbering, attached to the word before them; each subpage's reference list, which the transcription prints after the subpage's text, became one paragraph per note in Project Gutenberg's form [Footnote n: text], its paragraphs and line breaks joined with single spaces (a note that runs on from one scan page to the next is one note, its continuation marker dropped).
